values: Materials and setup | All fictional, paper and pencil only

You organize patterns and inspection records for a fictional two-piece leather component, using only paper, a pencil, and a ruler; do not cut leather or use needles, machines, or adhesives. The dimensions and tolerances are set for this problem, not production standards.

A1 | Both pieces are rectangular finished 80×50 mm, with a 5 mm allowance added on each of the four sides of each piece. Calculate the cut piece dimensions for one piece and the theoretical minimum cutting area for two pieces, writing the units in both square millimeters and square centimeters.

A2 | The total available material area is only 100 square centimeters. Judge sufficiency based on area alone; real leather also requires avoiding defects, checking grain, and marking the layout, so a sufficient area does not guarantee it can be laid out.

A3 | The four markings on the same paper line should be 10, 20, 30, and 40 mm, and the recorded readings are 10, 20, 33, and 40 mm. The tolerance for this problem is ±1 mm; write the deviation of each point and the nonconforming positions.

A4 | A fictional customer says the shoe sole has partially separated, the material is unknown, and there is no brand process or hidden damage information. Write the known, unknown, to-be-confirmed, and responsibility handoff in the intake form, and do not decide the adhesive or guarantee repairability.

A5 | Output the two-piece pattern dimension table, area calculation, marking inspection form, and intake form. The pattern only draws the outline and dimensions and is not actually cut; this problem provides no material formulation or medical advice.
Tasks and outputs
Deliver the A1—A3 dimensions and inspection table, listing finished size, allowance, cut piece, area, available area, deviation, and conformity judgment, retaining units and the problem numbers.

Also submit the A4 intake record: product, description, unknown materials, damage scope to be checked, inspection owner, and next steps after confirmation; do not write the candidate plan as approved.
Reference answer | Complete it independently first

A1 cut piece (80+2×5)×(50+2×5)=90×60 mm; one piece 5400 square millimeters, two pieces 10800 square millimeters = 108 square centimeters. A2 is short by at least 108−100=8 square centimeters, so the area is already insufficient.

A3 the four point deviations are 0, 0, +3, 0 mm; the third point exceeds ±1 mm and should be recorded as nonconforming with the original marking rechecked, and do not quietly change 33 to 30 and then call the original record conforming.

A4 only the customer's description of a partial sole separation is known, and the material and hidden damage are unknown. Hand to trained personnel to check the material, connection, and feasible scope, then confirm the plan and quote; do not choose an adhesive, do not guarantee restoration, and refer medical needs to the appropriate professionals.
Boundaries and review

Only paper dimensions and information records are made. The 108 square centimeter area is a theoretical minimum and excludes real layout waste; the ±1 mm in this problem is a teaching condition only. Check A1—A5 and all units, and keep materials, hidden damage, and unconfirmed craft items unknown.
